The two claims have different claimants who share the last name Morris.

**C-1094: Eric Morris**
- The name comes from the claim notes ("Claimant: Eric Morris", C-1094_adjuster_file.pdf, page 1).
- Date of loss: 2024-07-20, at an intersection. He reports a wrist fracture.
- 8 treatment visits. Total paid so far: 4,671.76.

**C-1199: Sarah Morris**
- The name comes from the first report of the loss ("Claimant name: Sarah Morris"). That report also lists the shared address, 12281 Williams Harbors Suite 229 (C-1199_fnol.pdf, page 1).
- Date of loss: 2024-09-27. It was a low-speed head-on crash in Pearland. She reports neck pain.
- 18 treatment visits. Total paid so far: 15,762.97.

**What they have in common:**
- The same address and the same policy, POL-0092.
- They are about two months apart, in separate accidents (I-0093 and I-0191).

**What may fit an ordinary explanation:**
- The shared last name and policy suggest they may live in the same household. That alone is not a fraud signal.

**Points that may need human review:**
- In both recorded statements, the claimant would not give their full name for the record (C-1094_adjuster_file.pdf, page 2; C-1199_adjuster_file.pdf, page 2).
- C-1094 lists Eric Morris as the driver of the other vehicle, but his claim sits on the same policy as his household. That needs a check.
- For C-1199, the adjuster notes that treatment "has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury" (C-1199_adjuster_file.pdf, page 1).

I can pull the fraud scores for both claims next.
